newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shinhan Bank seen reviving FRN issue.
newsitem.headline: Shinhan Bank seen reviving FRN issue.

text.p: Shinhan Bank is seen returning to the international debt market with a floating rate note issue, bankers said on Wednesday.
Bankers said the issuer is expected to come to the market in the first half of this year.
The issue size is likely to be US$200 million, or its equivalent in other currencies such as Japanese yen or British pounds.
The facility is expected to have a final maturity of three years with no put or call options. No formal mandate has not been awarded yet, bankers noted.
Shinhan Bank had verbally mandated Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and HSBC Markets in January of this year to arrange a three-year US$200 million floating rate note issue.
However, the issue was delayed after the default of Hanbo Steel sparked volatility in South Korea's domestic financial markets and unnerved international investors.
